newsitem.title: JAPAN: Former cult member admits shot Japan police chief.
newsitem.headline: Former cult member admits shot Japan police chief.

text.p: A policeman who belonged to the cult accused of last year's Tokyo subway gas attack has confessed to shooting Japan's police chief at the height of probes into the sect, a government spokesman said on Friday.
The spokesman told reporters the 31-year-old man had not been arrested and was still being questioned by police.
National Police Agency chief Takaji Kunimatsu was shot as he left his home on March 30, 1995, 10 days after sarin nerve gas was released in Tokyo's subway system during the morning rush hour.

Kunimatsu was shot four times from about 20 metres (yards) away by a masked man as he left his Tokyo apartment building. After spending three months in hospital, he resumed his duties and is still Japan's police chief.

Police have blamed doomsday cult Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect) for the subway gas attack, which killed 12 people and made about 6,000 ill. The sect's guru, Shoko Asahara, and about 100 cult members are on trial for the attack.
The policeman referred to was in a special team investigating the subway attack, but was removed from the group after his name was found on a list of sect members.
Police sources said investigators suspect the man carried out the attack on the police chief to disrupt the investigation into the subway attack.
Police had been questioning him for nearly six months prior to his confession.
